old_caption: The video captures a serene landscape scene at what appears to be sunrise or sunset, characterized by a tranquil river flowing through a valley. The river is calm, reflecting the soft hues of the sky and the surrounding mountains. On either side of the river, there are dense forests of tall trees, some with autumnal colors, suggesting the season might be fall. The mountains in the background are majestic, with one prominent peak on the left and another on the right, both partially shrouded in mist. The sky transitions from a deep blue at the top to a warm orange near the horizon, indicating the time of day. There are no visible animals or people in the scene, emphasizing the untouched beauty of nature. The camera remains stationary throughout the video, allowing viewers to fully absorb the peaceful and picturesque setting.

caption: The video captures a wide, eye-level view of Yosemite Valley bathed in the soft pastel light of twilight, where a calm river fills the foreground and mirrors the sky and cliffs above. On the left, a towering granite face glows with a warm orange alpenglow band near its upper edge, while leafy trees at the bank cast dark, steady reflections into the still water. To the right, blue-grey rock formations rise behind a line of conifers, their silhouettes held firm against the lavender sky. A horizontal band of reddish-gold meadow shrubs and small trees crosses the middle ground, separating the water from the distant peaks. Scattered rocks break the surface in the lower right and center, their shapes remaining unchanged throughout. The water's reflection of the cliffs and sky stays glassy and undisturbed across the clip. The lighting and composition hold a quiet, motionless balance for the entire visible duration.

An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.

camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.

processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.
